01.c360543ce1:
<n>18:2</n> Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum ejus annúntiat firmaméntum.
<n>18:3</n> Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.
<n>18:4</n> Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.
<n>18:5</n> In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
<n>18:6</n> In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:
<n>18:6</n> Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio ejus:
<n>18:7</n> Et occúrsus ejus usque ad summum ejus: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre ejus.
<n>18:8</n> Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.
<n>18:9</n> Justítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.
<n>18:10</n> Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * judícia Dómini vera, justificáta in semetípsa.
<n>18:11</n> Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.
<n>18:12</n> Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.
<n>18:13</n> Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
<n>18:14</n> Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.
<n>18:15</n> Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.
<n>18:15</n> Dómine, adjútor meus, * et redémptor meus.
01.1acf8d4923:
<n>18:2</n> The heavens shew forth the glory of God, * and the firmament declareth the work of his hands.
<n>18:3</n> Day to day uttereth speech, * and night to night sheweth knowledge.
<n>18:4</n> There are no speeches nor languages, * where their voices are not heard.
<n>18:5</n> Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth: * and their words unto the ends of the world.
<n>18:6</n> He hath set his tabernacle in the sun: * and he, as a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber,
<n>18:6</n> Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way: * his going out is from the end of heaven,
<n>18:7</n> And his circuit even to the end thereof: * and there is no one that can hide himself from his heat.
<n>18:8</n> The law of the Lord is unspotted, converting souls: * the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones.
<n>18:9</n> The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: * the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.
<n>18:10</n> The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: * the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.
<n>18:11</n> More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.
<n>18:12</n> For thy servant keepeth them, * and in keeping them there is a great reward.
<n>18:13</n> Who can understand sins? from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord: * and from those of others spare thy servant.
<n>18:14</n> If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot: * and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.
<n>18:15</n> And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: * and the meditation of my heart always in thy sight.
<n>18:15</n> O Lord, my helper, * and my redeemer.
01.f65d2884b5:
<n>13:1</n> Magnus es, Dómine, in ætérnum, * et in ómnia sǽcula regnum tuum:
<n>13:2</n> Quóniam tu flagéllas, et salvas: dedúcis ad ínferos, et redúcis: * et non est qui effúgiat manum tuam.
<n>13:3</n> Confitémini Dómino, fílii Israël, * et in conspéctu géntium laudáte eum:
<n>13:4</n> Quóniam ídeo dispérsit vos inter gentes, quæ ignórant eum, * ut vos enarrétis mirabília ejus,
<n>13:5</n> Et faciátis scire eos, * quia non est álius Deus omnípotens præter eum.
<n>13:6</n> Ipse castigávit nos propter iniquitátes nostras: * et ipse salvábit nos propter misericórdiam suam.
<n>13:7</n> Aspícite ergo quæ fecit nobíscum, et cum timóre et tremóre confitémini illi: * Regémque sæculórum exaltáte in opéribus vestris.
<n>13:8</n> Ego autem in terra captivitátis meæ confitébor illi: * quóniam osténdit majestátem suam in gentem peccatrícem.
<n>13:9</n> Convertímini ítaque, peccatóres, et fácite justítiam coram Deo, * credéntes quod fáciat vobíscum misericórdiam suam:
<n>13:10</n> Ego autem, et ánima mea * in eo lætábimur.
<n>13:11</n> Benedícite Dóminum, omnes elécti ejus: * ágite dies lætítiæ, et confitémini illi.
01.38b78cfa76:
<n>13:1</n> Thou art great, O Lord, for ever, * and thy kingdom is unto all ages:
<n>13:2</n> For thou scourgest, and thou savest: thou leadest down to hell, and bringest up again: * and there is none that can escape thy hand.
<n>13:3</n> Give glory to the Lord, ye children of Israel, * and praise him in the sight of the Gentiles:
<n>13:4</n> Because he hath therefore scattered you among the Gentiles, who know not him, * that you may declare his wonderful works,
<n>13:5</n> And make them know * that there is no other almighty God besides him.
<n>13:6</n> He hath chastised us for our iniquities: * and he will save us for his own mercy.
<n>13:7</n> See then what he hath done with us, and with fear and trembling give ye glory to him: * and extol the eternal King of worlds in your works.
<n>13:8</n> As for me, I will praise him in the land of my captivity: * because he hath shewn his majesty toward a sinful nation.
<n>13:9</n> Be converted therefore, ye sinners, and do justice before God, * believing that he will shew his mercy to you.
<n>13:10</n> And I and my soul * will rejoice in him.
<n>13:11</n> Bless ye the Lord, all his elect, * keep days of joy, and give glory to him.
01.189a63e7a0:
<n>11:2</n> Salvum me fac, Dómine, quóniam defécit sanctus: * quóniam diminútæ sunt veritátes a fíliis hóminum.
<n>11:3</n> Vana locúti sunt unusquísque ad próximum suum: * lábia dolósa, in corde et corde locúti sunt.
<n>11:4</n> Dispérdat Dóminus univérsa lábia dolósa, * et linguam magníloquam.
<n>11:5</n> Qui dixérunt: Linguam nostram magnificábimus, lábia nostra a nobis sunt, * quis noster Dóminus est?
<n>11:6</n> Propter misériam ínopum, et gémitum páuperum, * nunc exsúrgam, dicit Dóminus.
<n>11:6</n> Ponam in salutári: * fiduciáliter agam in eo.
<n>11:7</n> Elóquia Dómini, elóquia casta: * argéntum igne examinátum, probátum terræ purgátum séptuplum.
<n>11:8</n> Tu, Dómine, servábis nos: et custódies nos * a generatióne hac in ætérnum.
<n>11:9</n> In circúitu ímpii ámbulant: * secúndum altitúdinem tuam multiplicásti fílios hóminum.
01.42c5e68645:
<n>11:2</n> Save me, O Lord, for there is now no saint: * truths are decayed from among the children of men.
<n>11:3</n> They have spoken vain things every one to his neighbour: * with deceitful lips, and with a double heart have they spoken.
<n>11:4</n> May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips, * and the tongue that speaketh proud things.
<n>11:5</n> Who have said: We will magnify our tongue; our lips are our own; * who is Lord over us?
<n>11:6</n> By reason of the misery of the needy, and the groans of the poor, * now will I arise, saith the Lord.
<n>11:6</n> I will set him in safety; * I will deal confidently in his regard.
<n>11:7</n> The words of the Lord are pure words: * as silver tried by the fire, purged from the earth, refined seven times.
<n>11:8</n> Thou, O Lord, wilt preserve us: and keep us * from this generation for ever.
<n>11:9</n> The wicked walk round about: * according to thy highness, thou hast multiplied the children of men.
01.92d75a754c:
<n>12:1</n> Úsquequo, Dómine, obliviscéris me in finem? * Úsquequo avértis fáciem tuam a me?
<n>12:2</n> Quámdiu ponam consília in ánima mea, * dolórem in corde meo per diem?
<n>12:3</n> Úsquequo exaltábitur inimícus meus super me? * réspice, et exáudi me, Dómine, Deus meus.
<n>12:4</n> Illúmina óculos meos ne umquam obdórmiam in morte: * nequándo dicat inimícus meus: Præválui advérsus eum.
<n>12:5</n> Qui tríbulant me, exsultábunt si motus fúero: * ego autem in misericórdia tua sperávi.
<n>12:6</n> Exsultábit cor meum in salutári tuo: cantábo Dómino qui bona tríbuit mihi: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.
01.e9306f9562:
<n>12:1</n> How long, O Lord, wilt thou forget me unto the end? * how long dost thou turn away thy face from me?
<n>12:2</n> How long shall I take counsels in my soul, * sorrow in my heart all the day?
<n>12:3</n> How long shall my enemy be exalted over me? * Consider, and hear me, O Lord my God.
<n>12:4</n> Enlighten my eyes that I never sleep in death: * lest at any time my enemy say: I have prevailed against him.
<n>12:5</n> They that trouble me will rejoice when I am moved: * but I have trusted in thy mercy.
<n>12:6</n> My heart shall rejoice in thy salvation: I will sing to the Lord, who giveth me good things: * yea, I will sing to the name of the Lord the most High.
01.fa58304b89:
<n>15:1</n> Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. * Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.
<n>15:3</n> Sanctis, qui sunt in terra ejus, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.
<n>15:4</n> Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: * póstea acceleravérunt.
<n>15:4</n> Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, * nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.
<n>15:5</n> Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: * tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.
<n>15:6</n> Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.
<n>15:7</n> Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: * ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.
<n>15:8</n> Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: * quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.
<n>15:9</n> Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: * ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.
<n>15:10</n> Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: * nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.
<n>15:11</n> Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: * delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.
01.b8b7ae09cd:
<n>15:1</n> Preserve me, O Lord, for I have put my trust in thee. * I have said to the Lord, thou art my God, for thou hast no need of my goods.
<n>15:3</n> To the saints, who are in his land, * he hath made wonderful all my desires in them.
<n>15:4</n> Their infirmities were multiplied: * afterwards they made haste.
<n>15:4</n> I will not gather together their meetings for blood offerings: * nor will I be mindful of their names by my lips.
<n>15:5</n> The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup: * it is thou that wilt restore my inheritance to me.
<n>15:6</n> The lines are fallen unto me in goodly places: * for my inheritance is goodly to me.
<n>15:7</n> I will bless the Lord, who hath given me understanding: * moreover my reins also have corrected me even till night.
<n>15:8</n> I set the Lord always in my sight: * for he is at my right hand, that I be not moved.
<n>15:9</n> Therefore my heart hath been glad, and my tongue hath rejoiced: * moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope.
<n>15:10</n> Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; * nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption.
<n>15:11</n> Thou hast made known to me the ways of life, thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance: * at thy right hand are delights even to the end.
01.fd989081d9:
<n>16:15</n> Hymnum cantémus Dómino, * hymnum novum cantémus Deo nostro.
<n>16:16</n> Adonái, Dómine, magnus es tu, et præclárus in virtúte tua, * et quem superáre nemo potest.
<n>16:17</n> Tibi sérviat omnis creatúra tua: * quia dixísti, et facta sunt:
<n>16:18</n> Misísti spíritum tuum, et creáta sunt, * et non est qui resístat voci tuæ.
<n>16:19</n> Montes a fundaméntis movebúntur cum aquis: * petræ, sicut cera, liquéscent ante fáciem tuam.
<n>16:20</n> Qui autem timent te, * magni erunt apud te per ómnia.
<n>16:21</n> Væ genti insurgénti super genus meum: Dóminus enim omnípotens vindicábit in eis, * in die judícii visitábit illos.
<n>16:22</n> Dabit enim ignem, et vermes in carnes eórum, * ut urántur, et séntiant usque in sempitérnum.
01.95f908f40c:
<n>16:15</n> Let us sing a hymn to the Lord, * let us sing a new hymn to our God.
<n>16:16</n> O Adonai, Lord, great art thou, and glorious in thy power, * and no one can overcome thee.
<n>16:17</n> Let all thy creatures serve thee: * because thou hast spoken, and they were made:
<n>16:18</n> Thou didst send forth thy spirit, and they were created, * and there is no one that can resist thy voice.
<n>16:19</n> The mountains shall be moved from the foundations with the waters: * the rocks shall melt as wax before thy face.
<n>16:20</n> But they that fear thee, * shall be great with thee in all things.
<n>16:21</n> Woe be to the nation that riseth up against my people: for the Lord almighty will take revenge on them, * in the day of judgment he will visit them.
<n>16:22</n> For he will give fire, and worms into their flesh, * that they may burn, and may feel for ever.
01.8b464eaed3:
<n>10:2</n> In Dómino confído: quómodo dícitis ánimæ meæ: * Tránsmigra in montem sicut passer?
<n>10:3</n> Quóniam ecce peccatóres intendérunt arcum, paravérunt sagíttas suas in pháretra, * ut sagíttent in obscúro rectos corde.
<n>10:4</n> Quóniam quæ perfecísti, destruxérunt: * justus autem quid fecit?
<n>10:5</n> Dóminus in templo sancto suo, * Dóminus in cælo sedes ejus.
<n>10:5</n> Óculi ejus in páuperem respíciunt: * pálpebræ ejus intérrogant fílios hóminum.
<n>10:6</n> Dóminus intérrogat justum et ímpium: * qui autem díligit iniquitátem, odit ánimam suam.
<n>10:7</n> Pluet super peccatóres láqueos: * ignis, et sulphur, et spíritus procellárum pars cálicis eórum.
<n>10:8</n> Quóniam justus Dóminus, et justítias diléxit: * æquitátem vidit vultus ejus.
01.746a0a337f:
<n>10:2</n> In the Lord I put my trust: how then do you say to my soul: * Get thee away from hence to the mountain, like a sparrow?
<n>10:3</n> For, lo, the wicked have bent their bow: they have prepared their arrows in the quiver, * to shoot in the dark the upright of heart.
<n>10:4</n> For they have destroyed the things which thou hast made: * but what has the just man done?
<n>10:5</n> The Lord is in his holy temple, * the Lord’s throne is in heaven.
<n>10:5</n> His eyes look on the poor man: * his eyelids examine the sons of men.
<n>10:6</n> The Lord trieth the just and the wicked: * but he that loveth iniquity, hateth his own soul.
<n>10:7</n> He shall rain snares upon sinners: * fire and brimstone, and storms of winds, shall be the portion of their cup.
<n>10:8</n> For the Lord is just, and hath loved justice: * his countenance hath beheld righteousness.

<n>18:9</n> The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: * the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.
<n>18:10</n> The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: * the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.
<n>18:11</n> More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.
<n>18:12</n> For thy servant keepeth them, * and in keeping them there is a great reward.
<n>18:13</n> Who can understand sins? from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord: * and from those of others spare thy servant.
<n>18:14</n> If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot: * and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.
<n>18:15</n> And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: * and the meditation of my heart always in thy sight.
<n>18:15</n> O Lord, my helper, * and my redeemer.
01.baed7a2369:
<n>14:1</n> Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?
<n>14:2</n> Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur justítiam:
<n>14:3</n> Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:
<n>14:3</n> Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.
<n>14:4</n> Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu ejus malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:
<n>14:4</n> Qui jurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.
<n>14:5</n> Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.
01.b202b85310:
<n>14:1</n> Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? * or who shall rest in thy holy hill?
<n>14:2</n> He that walketh without blemish, * and worketh justice:
<n>14:3</n> He that speaketh truth in his heart, * who hath not used deceit in his tongue:
<n>14:3</n> Nor hath done evil to his neighbour: * nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.
<n>14:4</n> In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: * but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord:
<n>14:4</n> He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth not; * He that hath not put out his money to usury, nor taken bribes against the innocent:
<n>14:5</n> He that doth these things, * shall not be moved for ever.
01.c1c85ce4a8:
<n>13:1</n> Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * non est Deus.
<n>13:1</n> Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in stúdiis suis: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
<n>13:2</n> Dóminus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum, * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.
<n>13:3</n> Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
<n>13:3</n> Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum: linguis suis dolóse agébant * venénum áspidum sub lábiis eórum.
<n>13:3</n> Quorum os maledictióne et amaritúdine plenum est: * velóces pedes eórum ad effundéndum sánguinem.
<n>13:3</n> Contrítio et infelícitas in viis eórum, et viam pacis non cognovérunt: * non est timor Dei ante óculos eórum.
<n>13:4</n> Nonne cognóscent omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam sicut escam panis?
<n>13:5</n> Dóminum non invocavérunt, * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.
<n>13:6</n> Quóniam Dóminus in generatióne justa est, consílium ínopis confudístis: * quóniam Dóminus spes ejus est.
<n>13:7</n> Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum avérterit Dóminus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Jacob, et lætábitur Israël.
01.f83f40ea25:
<n>13:1</n> The fool hath said in his heart: * there is no God.
<n>13:1</n> They are corrupt, and are become abominable in their ways: * there is none that doth good, no not one.
<n>13:2</n> The Lord hath looked down from heaven upon the children of men, * to see if there be any that understand and seek God.
<n>13:3</n> They are all gone aside, they are become unprofitable together: * there is none that doth good: no not one.
<n>13:3</n> Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they acted deceitfully: * the poison of asps is under their lips.
<n>13:3</n> Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness; * their feet are swift to shed blood.
<n>13:3</n> Destruction and unhappiness in their ways; and the way of peace they have not known: * there is no fear of God before their eyes.
<n>13:4</n> Shall not all they know that work iniquity, * who devour my people as they eat bread?
<n>13:5</n> They have not called upon the Lord: * there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.
<n>13:6</n> For the Lord is in the just generation: you have confounded the counsel of the poor man; * but the Lord is his hope.
<n>13:7</n> Who shall give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when the Lord shall have turned away the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
01.04177af536:
<n>16:1</n> Exáudi, Dómine, justítiam meam: * inténde deprecatiónem meam.
<n>16:1</n> Áuribus pércipe oratiónem meam, * non in lábiis dolósis.
<n>16:2</n> De vultu tuo judícium meum pródeat: * óculi tui vídeant æquitátes.
<n>16:3</n> Probásti cor meum, et visitásti nocte: * igne me examinásti, et non est invénta in me iníquitas.
<n>16:4</n> Ut non loquátur os meum ópera hóminum: * propter verba labiórum tuórum ego custodívi vias duras.
<n>16:5</n> Pérfice gressus meos in sémitis tuis: * ut non moveántur vestígia mea.
<n>16:6</n> Ego clamávi, quóniam exaudísti me, Deus: * inclína aurem tuam mihi, et exáudi verba mea.
<n>16:7</n> Mirífica misericórdias tuas, * qui salvos facis sperántes in te.
<n>16:8</n> A resisténtibus déxteræ tuæ custódi me, * ut pupíllam óculi.
<n>16:8</n> Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege me: * a fácie impiórum qui me afflixérunt.
<n>16:9</n> Inimíci mei ánimam meam circumdedérunt, ádipem suum conclusérunt: * os eórum locútum est supérbiam.
<n>16:11</n> Proiciéntes me nunc circumdedérunt me: * óculos suos statuérunt declináre in terram.
<n>16:12</n> Suscepérunt me sicut leo parátus ad prædam: * et sicut cátulus leónis hábitans in ábditis.
<n>16:13</n> Exsúrge, Dómine, prǽveni eum, et supplánta eum: * éripe ánimam meam ab ímpio, frámeam tuam ab inimícis manus tuæ.
<n>16:14</n> Dómine, a paucis de terra dívide eos in vita eórum: * de abscónditis tuis adimplétus est venter eórum.
<n>16:14</n> Saturáti sunt fíliis: * et dimisérunt relíquias suas párvulis suis.
<n>16:15</n> Ego autem in justítia apparébo conspéctui tuo: * satiábor cum apparúerit glória tua.
01.85e0e3178f:
<n>16:1</n> Hear, O Lord, my justice: * attend to my supplication.
<n>16:1</n> Give ear unto my prayer, * which proceedeth not from deceitful lips.
<n>16:2</n> Let my judgment come forth from thy countenance: * let thy eyes behold the things that are equitable.
<n>16:3</n> Thou hast proved my heart, and visited it by night, * thou hast tried me by fire: and iniquity hath not been found in me.
<n>16:4</n> That my mouth may not speak the works of men: * for the sake of the words of thy lips, I have kept hard ways.
<n>16:5</n> Perfect thou my goings in thy paths: * that my footsteps be not moved.
<n>16:6</n> I have cried to thee, for thou, O God, hast heard me: * O incline thy ear unto me, and hear my words.
<n>16:7</n> Shew forth thy wonderful mercies; * thou who savest them that trust in thee.
<n>16:8</n> From them that resist thy right hand keep me, * as the apple of thy eye.
<n>16:8</n> Protect me under the shadow of thy wings: * from the face of the wicked who have afflicted me.
<n>16:9</n> My enemies have surrounded my soul: They have shut up their fat: * their mouth hath spoken proudly.
<n>16:11</n> They have cast me forth, and now they have surrounded me: * they have set their eyes bowing down to the earth.
<n>16:12</n> They have taken me, as a lion prepared for the prey; * and as a young lion dwelling in secret places.
<n>16:13</n> Arise, O Lord, disappoint him and supplant him; * deliver my soul from the wicked one; thy sword from the enemies of thy hand.
<n>16:14</n> O Lord, divide them from the few of the earth in their life: * their belly is filled from thy hidden stores.
<n>16:14</n> They are full of children: * and they have left to their little ones the rest of their substance.
<n>16:15</n> But as for me, I will appear before thy sight in justice: * I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear.
01.ab8ee5d5a7:
<n>17:2</n> Díligam te, Dómine, fortitúdo mea: * Dóminus firmaméntum meum, et refúgium meum, et liberátor meus.
<n>17:3</n> Deus meus adjútor meus, * et sperábo in eum.
<n>17:3</n> Protéctor meus, et cornu salútis meæ, * et suscéptor meus.
<n>17:4</n> Laudans invocábo Dóminum: * et ab inimícis meis salvus ero.
<n>17:5</n> Circumdedérunt me dolóres mortis: * et torréntes iniquitátis conturbavérunt me.
<n>17:6</n> Dolóres inférni circumdedérunt me: * præoccupavérunt me láquei mortis.
<n>17:7</n> In tribulatióne mea invocávi Dóminum, * et ad Deum meum clamávi.
<n>17:7</n> Et exaudívit de templo sancto suo vocem meam: * et clamor meus in conspéctu ejus, introívit in aures ejus.
<n>17:8</n> Commóta est, et contrémuit terra: * fundaménta móntium conturbáta sunt, et commóta sunt, quóniam irátus est eis.
<n>17:9</n> Ascéndit fumus in ira ejus: et ignis a fácie ejus exársit: * carbónes succénsi sunt ab eo.
<n>17:10</n> Inclinávit cælos, et descéndit: * et calígo sub pédibus ejus.
<n>17:11</n> Et ascéndit super Chérubim, et volávit: * volávit super pennas ventórum.
<n>17:12</n> Et pósuit ténebras latíbulum suum, in circúitu ejus tabernáculum ejus: * tenebrósa aqua in núbibus áëris.
<n>17:13</n> Præ fulgóre in conspéctu ejus nubes transiérunt, * grando et carbónes ignis.
<n>17:14</n> Et intónuit de cælo Dóminus, et Altíssimus dedit vocem suam: * grando et carbónes ignis.
<n>17:15</n> Et misit sagíttas suas, et dissipávit eos: * fúlgura multiplicávit, et conturbávit eos.
<n>17:16</n> Et apparuérunt fontes aquárum, * et reveláta sunt fundaménta orbis terrárum:
<n>17:16</n> Ab increpatióne tua, Dómine, * ab inspiratióne spíritus iræ tuæ.
01.cfad036467:
<n>17:2</n> I will love thee, O Lord, my strength: * The Lord is my firmament, my refuge, and my deliverer.
<n>17:3</n> My God is my helper, * and in him will I put my trust.
<n>17:3</n> My protector, and the horn of my salvation, * and my support.
<n>17:4</n> Praising, I will call upon the Lord: * and I shall be saved from my enemies.
<n>17:5</n> The sorrows of death surrounded me: * and the torrents of iniquity troubled me.
<n>17:6</n> The sorrows of hell encompassed me: * and the snares of death prevented me.
<n>17:7</n> In my affliction I called upon the Lord, * and I cried to my God:
<n>17:7</n> And he heard my voice from his holy temple: * and my cry before him came into his ears.
<n>17:8</n> The earth shook and trembled: * the foundations of the mountains were troubled and were moved, because he was angry with them.
<n>17:9</n> There went up a smoke in his wrath: and a fire flamed from his face: * coals were kindled by it.
<n>17:10</n> He bowed the heavens, and came down, * and darkness was under his feet.
<n>17:11</n> And he ascended upon the cherubim, and he flew; * he flew upon the wings of the winds.
<n>17:12</n> And he made darkness his covert, his pavilion round about him: * dark waters in the clouds of the air.
<n>17:13</n> At the brightness that was before him the clouds passed, * hail and coals of fire.
<n>17:14</n> And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Highest gave his voice: * hail and coals of fire.
<n>17:15</n> And he sent forth his arrows, and he scattered them: * he multiplied lightnings, and troubled them.
<n>17:16</n> Then the fountains of waters appeared, * and the foundations of the world were discovered:
<n>17:16</n> At thy rebuke, O Lord, * at the blast of the spirit of thy wrath.
01.cb121c7514:
<n>17:17</n> Misit de summo, et accépit me: * et assúmpsit me de aquis multis.
<n>17:18</n> Erípuit me de inimícis meis fortíssimis, et ab his qui odérunt me: * quóniam confortáti sunt super me.
<n>17:19</n> Prævenérunt me in die afflictiónis meæ: * et factus est Dóminus protéctor meus.
<n>17:20</n> Et edúxit me in latitúdinem: * salvum me fecit, quóniam vóluit me.
<n>17:21</n> Et retríbuet mihi Dóminus secúndum justítiam meam: * et secúndum puritátem mánuum meárum retríbuet mihi:
<n>17:22</n> Quia custodívi vias Dómini, * nec ímpie gessi a Deo meo.
<n>17:23</n> Quóniam ómnia judícia ejus in conspéctu meo: * et justítias ejus non répuli a me.
<n>17:24</n> Et ero immaculátus cum eo: * et observábo me ab iniquitáte mea.
<n>17:25</n> Et retríbuet mihi Dóminus secúndum justítiam meam: * et secúndum puritátem mánuum meárum in conspéctu oculórum ejus.
<n>17:26</n> Cum sancto sanctus eris, * et cum viro innocénte ínnocens eris:
<n>17:27</n> Et cum elécto eléctus eris: * et cum pervérso pervertéris.
<n>17:28</n> Quóniam tu pópulum húmilem salvum fácies: * et óculos superbórum humiliábis.
<n>17:29</n> Quóniam tu illúminas lucérnam meam, Dómine: * Deus meus, illúmina ténebras meas.
<n>17:30</n> Quóniam in te erípiar a tentatióne, * et in Deo meo transgrédiar murum.
<n>17:31</n> Deus meus, impollúta via ejus: elóquia Dómini igne examináta: * protéctor est ómnium sperántium in se.
<n>17:32</n> Quóniam quis Deus præter Dóminum? * aut quis Deus præter Deum nostrum?
<n>17:33</n> Deus, qui præcínxit me virtúte: * et pósuit immaculátam viam meam.
<n>17:34</n> Qui perfécit pedes meos tamquam cervórum, * et super excélsa státuens me.
<n>17:35</n> Qui docet manus meas ad prǽlium: * et posuísti, ut arcum ǽreum, brácchia mea.
01.5294dec254:
<n>17:17</n> He sent from on high, and took me: * and received me out of many waters.
<n>17:18</n> He delivered me from my strongest enemies, and from them that hated me: * for they were too strong for me.
<n>17:19</n> They prevented me in the day of my affliction: * and the Lord became my protector.
<n>17:20</n> And he brought me forth into a large place: * he saved me, because he was well pleased with me.
<n>17:21</n> And the Lord will reward me according to my justice; * and will repay me according to the cleanness of my hands:
<n>17:22</n> Because I have kept the ways of the Lord; * and have not done wickedly against my God.
<n>17:23</n> For all his judgments are in my sight: * and his justices I have not put away from me.
<n>17:24</n> And I shall be spotless with him: * and shall keep myself from my iniquity.
<n>17:25</n> And the Lord will reward me according to my justice: * and according to the cleanness of my hands before his eyes.
<n>17:26</n> With the holy thou wilt be holy; * and with the innocent man thou wilt be innocent:
<n>17:27</n> And with the elect thou wilt be elect: * and with the perverse thou wilt be perverted.
<n>17:28</n> For thou wilt save the humble people; * but wilt bring down the eyes of the proud.
<n>17:29</n> For thou lightest my lamp, O Lord: * O my God, enlighten my darkness.
<n>17:30</n> For by thee I shall be delivered from temptation; * and through my God I shall go over a wall.
<n>17:31</n> As for my God, his way is undefiled: the words of the Lord are fire-tried: * he is the protector of all that trust in him.
<n>17:32</n> For who is God but the Lord? * or who is God but our God?
<n>17:33</n> God, who hath girt me with strength; * and made my way blameless.
<n>17:34</n> Who hath made my feet like the feet of harts: * and who setteth me upon high places.
<n>17:35</n> Who teacheth my hands to war: * and thou hast made my arms like a brazen bow.
01.f263b1ffba:
<n>17:36</n> Et dedísti mihi protectiónem salútis tuæ: * et déxtera tua suscépit me:
<n>17:36</n> Et disciplína tua corréxit me in finem: * et disciplína tua ipsa me docébit.
<n>17:37</n> Dilatásti gressus meos subtus me: * et non sunt infirmáta vestígia mea:
<n>17:38</n> Pérsequar inimícos meos et comprehéndam illos: * et non convértar, donec defíciant.
<n>17:39</n> Confríngam illos, nec póterunt stare: * cadent subtus pedes meos.
<n>17:40</n> Et præcinxísti me virtúte ad bellum: * et supplantásti insurgéntes in me subtus me.
<n>17:41</n> Et inimícos meos dedísti mihi dorsum, * et odiéntes me disperdidísti.
<n>17:42</n> Clamavérunt, nec erat qui salvos fáceret ad Dóminum: * nec exaudívit eos.
<n>17:43</n> Et commínuam eos, ut púlverem ante fáciem venti: * ut lutum plateárum delébo eos.
<n>17:44</n> Erípies me de contradictiónibus pópuli: * constítues me in caput géntium.
<n>17:45</n> Pópulus quem non cognóvi servívit mihi: * in audítu auris obedívit mihi.
<n>17:46</n> Fílii aliéni mentíti sunt mihi, * fílii aliéni inveteráti sunt, et claudicavérunt a sémitis suis.
<n>17:47</n> Vivit Dóminus, et benedíctus Deus meus: * et exaltétur Deus salútis meæ.
<n>17:48</n> Deus, qui das vindíctas mihi, et subdis pópulos sub me: * liberátor meus de inimícis meis iracúndis.
<n>17:49</n> Et ab insurgéntibus in me exaltábis me: * a viro iníquo erípies me.
<n>17:50</n> Proptérea confitébor tibi in natiónibus, Dómine: * et nómini tuo psalmum dicam.
<n>17:51</n> Magníficans salútes Regis ejus, et fáciens misericórdiam Christo suo David: * et sémini ejus usque in sǽculum.
01.833cad0641:
<n>17:36</n> Thou hast given me the protection of thy salvation: * and thy right hand hath held me up:
<n>17:36</n> And thy discipline hath corrected me unto the end: * and thy discipline, the same shall teach me.
<n>17:37</n> Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; * and my feet are not weakened.
<n>17:38</n> I will pursue after my enemies, and overtake them: * and I will not turn again till they are consumed.
<n>17:39</n> I will break them, and they shall not be able to stand: * they shall fall under my feet.
<n>17:40</n> And thou hast girded me with strength unto battle; * and hast subdued under me them that rose up against me.
<n>17:41</n> And thou hast made my enemies turn their back upon me, * and hast destroyed them that hated me.
<n>17:42</n> They cried, but there was none to save them, to the Lord: * but he heard them not.
<n>17:43</n> And I shall beat them as small as the dust before the wind; * I shall bring them to nought, like the dirt in the streets.
<n>17:44</n> Thou wilt deliver me from the contradictions of the people; * thou wilt make me head of the Gentiles.
<n>17:45</n> A people which I knew not, hath served me: * at the hearing of the ear they have obeyed me.
<n>17:46</n> The children that are strangers have lied to me, * strange children have faded away, and have halted from their paths.
<n>17:47</n> The Lord liveth, and blessed be my God, * and let the God of my salvation be exalted.
<n>17:48</n> O God, who avengest me, and subduest the people under me, * my deliverer from my enraged enemies.
<n>17:49</n> And thou wilt lift me up above them that rise up against me: * from the unjust man thou wilt deliver me.
<n>17:50</n> Therefore will I give glory to thee, O Lord, among the nations, * and I will sing a psalm to thy name.
<n>17:51</n> Giving great deliverance to his king, and shewing mercy to David, his anointed: * and to his seed for ever.
01.0b1e017a2f:
<n>19:2</n> Exáudiat te Dóminus in die tribulatiónis: * prótegat te nomen Dei Jacob.
<n>19:3</n> Mittat tibi auxílium de sancto: * et de Sion tueátur te.
<n>19:4</n> Memor sit omnis sacrifícii tui: * et holocáustum tuum pingue fiat.
<n>19:5</n> Tríbuat tibi secúndum cor tuum: * et omne consílium tuum confírmet.
<n>19:6</n> Lætábimur in salutári tuo: * et in nómine Dei nostri magnificábimur.
<n>19:7</n> Ímpleat Dóminus omnes petitiónes tuas: * nunc cognóvi quóniam salvum fecit Dóminus Christum suum.
<n>19:7</n> Exáudiet illum de cælo sancto suo: * in potentátibus salus déxteræ ejus.
<n>19:8</n> Hi in cúrribus, et hi in equis: * nos autem in nómine Dómini, Dei nostri invocábimus.
<n>19:9</n> Ipsi obligáti sunt, et cecidérunt: * nos autem surréximus et erécti sumus.
<n>19:10</n> Dómine, salvum fac regem: * et exáudi nos in die, qua invocavérimus te.
01.7a4fd53505:
<n>19:2</n> May the Lord hear thee in the day of tribulation: * may the name of the God of Jacob protect thee.
<n>19:3</n> May he send thee help from the sanctuary: * and defend thee out of Sion.
<n>19:4</n> May he be mindful of all thy sacrifices: * and may thy whole burnt offering be made fat.
<n>19:5</n> May he give thee according to thy own heart; * and confirm all thy counsels.
<n>19:6</n> We will rejoice in thy salvation; * and in the name of our God we shall be exalted.
<n>19:7</n> The Lord fulfil all thy petitions: * now have I known that the Lord hath saved his anointed.
<n>19:7</n> He will hear him from his holy heaven: * the salvation of his right hand is in powers.
<n>19:8</n> Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: * but we will call upon the name of the Lord, our God.
<n>19:9</n> They are bound, and have fallen: * but we are risen, and are set upright.
<n>19:10</n> O Lord, save the king: * and hear us in the day that we shall call upon thee.
01.7533c91b6a:
<n>15:1</n> Cantémus Dómino: glorióse enim magnificátus est, * equum et ascensórem dejécit in mare.
<n>15:2</n> Fortitúdo mea, et laus mea Dóminus, * et factus est mihi in salútem.
<n>15:3</n> Iste Deus meus, et glorificábo eum: * Deus patris mei, et exaltábo eum.
<n>15:4</n> Dóminus quasi vir pugnátor, Omnípotens nomen ejus. * Currus Pharaónis et exércitum ejus projécit in mare.
<n>15:5</n> Elécti príncipes ejus submérsi sunt in Mari Rubro: * abýssi operuérunt eos, descendérunt in profúndum quasi lapis.
<n>15:6</n> Déxtera tua, Dómine, magnificáta est in fortitúdine: déxtera tua, Dómine, percússit inimícum. * Et in multitúdine glóriæ tuæ deposuísti adversários tuos:
<n>15:7</n> Misísti iram tuam, quæ devorávit eos sicut stípulam. * Et in spíritu furóris tui congregátæ sunt aquæ:
<n>15:8</n> Stetit unda fluens, * congregátæ sunt abýssi in médio mari.
<n>15:9</n> Dixit inimícus: Pérsequar et comprehéndam, * dívidam spólia, implébitur ánima mea:
<n>15:10</n> Evaginábo gládium meum, * interfíciet eos manus mea.
<n>15:11</n> Flavit spíritus tuus, et opéruit eos mare: * submérsi sunt quasi plumbum in aquis veheméntibus.
<n>15:12</n> Quis símilis tui in fórtibus, Dómine? * quis símilis tui, magníficus in sanctitáte, terríbilis atque laudábilis, fáciens mirabília?
<n>15:13</n> Extendísti manum tuam, et devorávit eos terra. * Dux fuísti in misericórdia tua pópulo quem redemísti:
<n>15:14</n> Et portásti eum in fortitúdine tua, * ad habitáculum sanctum tuum.
<n>15:15</n> Ascendérunt pópuli, et iráti sunt: * dolóres obtinuérunt habitatóres Philísthiim.
<n>15:16</n> Tunc conturbáti sunt príncipes Edom, robústos Moab obtínuit tremor: * obriguérunt omnes habitatóres Chánaan.
<n>15:17</n> Írruat super eos formído et pavor, * in magnitúdine brácchii tui:
<n>15:18</n> Fiant immóbiles quasi lapis, donec pertránseat pópulus tuus, Dómine, * donec pertránseat pópulus tuus iste, quem possedísti.
<n>15:19</n> Introdúces eos, et plantábis in monte hereditátis tuæ, * firmíssimo habitáculo tuo quod operátus es, Dómine:
<n>15:20</n> Sanctuárium tuum, Dómine, quod firmavérunt manus tuæ. * Dóminus regnábit in ætérnum et ultra.
<n>15:21</n> Ingréssus est enim eques Phárao cum cúrribus et equítibus ejus in mare: * et redúxit super eos Dóminus aquas maris:
<n>15:22</n> Fílii autem Israël ambulavérunt per siccum * in médio ejus.
01.589b40bc1c:
<n>15:1</n> Let us sing to the Lord: for he is gloriously magnified, * the horse and the rider he hath thrown into the sea.
<n>15:2</n> The Lord is my strength and my praise, * and he is become salvation to me:
<n>15:3</n> He is my God and I will glorify him: * the God of my father, and I will exalt him.
<n>15:4</n> The Lord is as a man of war, Almighty is his name. * Pharao’s chariots and his army he hath cast into the sea:
<n>15:5</n> His chosen captains are drowned in the Red Sea. * The depths have covered them, they are sunk to the bottom like a stone.
<n>15:6</n> Thy right hand, O Lord, is magnified in strength: thy right hand, O Lord, hath slain the enemy. * And in the multitude of thy glory thou hast put down thy adversaries:
<n>15:7</n> Thou hast sent thy wrath, which hath devoured them like stubble. * And with the blast of thy anger the waters were gathered together:
<n>15:8</n> The flowing water stood, * the depths were gathered together in the midst of the sea.
<n>15:9</n> The enemy said: I will pursue and overtake, * I will divide the spoils, my soul shall have its fill:
<n>15:10</n> I will draw my sword, * my hand shall slay them.
<n>15:11</n> Thy wind blew and the sea covered them: * they sunk as lead in the mighty waters.
<n>15:12</n> Who is like to thee, among the strong, O Lord? * who is like to thee, glorious in holiness, terrible and praiseworthy, doing wonders?
<n>15:13</n> Thou stretchedst forth thy hand, and the earth swallowed them. * In thy mercy thou hast been a leader to the people which thou hast redeemed:
<n>15:14</n> And in thy strength thou hast carried them * to thy holy habitation.
<n>15:15</n> Nations rose up, and were angry: * sorrows took hold on the inhabitants of Philisthiim.
<n>15:16</n> Then were the princes of Edom troubled, trembling seized on the stout men of Moab: * all the inhabitants of Chanaan became stiff.
<n>15:17</n> Let fear and dread fall upon them, * in the greatness of thy arm:
<n>15:18</n> Let them become unmoveable as a stone, until thy people, O Lord, pass by: * until this thy people pass by, which thou hast possessed.
<n>15:19</n> Thou shalt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thy inheritance, * in thy most firm habitation which thou hast made, O Lord;
<n>15:20</n> Thy sanctuary, O Lord, which thy hands have established. * The Lord shall reign for ever and ever.
<n>15:21</n> For Pharao went in on horseback with his chariots and horsemen into the sea: * and the Lord brought back upon them the waters of the sea:
<n>15:22</n> But the children of Israel walked on dry ground * in the midst thereof.
01.27cb772260:
<n>12:1</n> Confitébor tibi, Dómine, quóniam irátus es mihi: * convérsus est furor tuus, et consolátus es me.
<n>12:2</n> Ecce Deus salvátor meus, * fiduciáliter agam, et non timébo:
<n>12:3</n> Quia fortitúdo mea, et laus mea Dóminus, * et factus est mihi in salútem.
<n>12:4</n> Hauriétis aquas in gáudio de fóntibus Salvatóris: * et dicétis in die illa: Confitémini Dómino, et invocáte nomen ejus:
<n>12:5</n> Notas fácite in pópulis adinventiónes ejus: * mementóte quóniam excélsum est nomen ejus.
<n>12:6</n> Cantáte Dómino quóniam magnífice fecit: * annuntiáte hoc in univérsa terra.
<n>12:7</n> Exsúlta, et lauda, habitátio Sion: * quia magnus in médio tui Sanctus Israël.
01.5c0da3c6cf:
<n>12:1</n> I will give thanks to thee, O Lord, for thou wast angry with me: * thy wrath is turned away, and thou hast comforted me.
<n>12:2</n> Behold, God is my saviour, * I will deal confidently, and will not fear:
<n>12:3</n> Because the Lord is my strength, and my praise, * and he is become my salvation.
<n>12:4</n> You shall draw waters with joy out of the saviour’s fountains: * And you shall say in that day: Praise ye the Lord, and call upon his name:
<n>12:5</n> Make his works known among the people: * remember that his name is high.
<n>12:6</n> Sing ye to the Lord, for he hath done great things: * shew this forth in all the earth.
<n>12:7</n> Rejoice, and praise, O thou habitation of Sion: * for great is he that is in the midst of thee the Holy One of Israel.
